market_holds: Spot $11.92 at the 2026-11-11 seal. That is -70.6% from the 52-week high, -15.9% over 20 days and +14.8% over 5 days. The 5-day rise is a drone-group bounce: KTOS, AVAV and RCAT fell together on 11/4-11/5 and rallied together on 11/6-11/9 (own arithmetic, Yahoo bars). The Nov-20 straddle prices 14.7% over 9 days. 20-day realised vol is 167%, so no separate event premium can be extracted. Skew is call-rich (25d put minus call = -15.9 vol points, 'upside paid'). The baseline lists one prior print (May, +1.7%) but misses the Q2 print, whose 8-K carried item 9.01 only. That print (2026-08-12, beat and raise) gapped -5.1% and closed -8.2% the next day. Consensus is inconsistent across sources. Earnings Whispers (2026-11-03) has Q3 revenue at $150.8M and EPS $0.09. Earnings Whispers beta has $121.5M, and Stock Alarm's snippet has $115M (5 analysts, $109-118M). The Q2 call said Q3 holds the smallest Deep Strike share, so the lower numbers fit the cadence. FY26 guide is $700-720M excluding BlackSea; BlackSea adds about $150M of FY26 revenue on a full-year basis and closed 2026-09-08. Street FY26 is about $760-764M including BlackSea; FY27 is $683M (Stock Alarm snippet, undated) versus Oppenheimer at $834M. Sell-side ratings are 10 Buy and 1 Hold, average target $25.80 (Investing.com). Targets were cut to $13 by Piper and UBS after the 2026-10-21 Bloomberg report that the Navy would stop buying the BlackSea GARC. The stock fell 32.5% that day. The company's 10-21 rebuttal says all 325 GARCs were delivered in 2025, none more were planned, and the contract runs to June 2027 at about $350M. The line the stock trades on is the first combined-company outlook: FY26 with BlackSea, any FY27 framework after the Deep Strike roll-off, book-to-bill and the BlackSea pipeline. Short interest is unavailable (NYSE listing; Nasdaq API refuses, MarketBeat 403).
view: This print is the first look at AEVEX with BlackSea consolidated, and it lands in the gap left by the Deep Strike roll-off. Q3 is the expected revenue trough. The FY26 guide will almost surely rise in headline terms because BlackSea is added mechanically, but the Street already carries BlackSea in FY26 (about $760M), so a raise to roughly $745-770M is in line, not a surprise. What decides the reaction is whatever management says about 2027: how much of the about $220M of 2026 Deep Strike revenue is replaced, whether BlackSea grows after GARC sustainment runs off mid-2027, and bookings under a continuing resolution. The independent evidence cuts both ways. Q3 awards announced since July add up to roughly a 1x book-to-bill: $88.1M (7/28), $41M (8/20), up to $92.2M (9/16) and $17.5M (7/6). The $41.6M mine-countermeasures award on 10/30 partly runs through the GARC contract, which supports the company's line that the GARC fleet is still being funded. Against that, the peer template this month is bad: Kratos beat Q3 but guided 2027 below expectations, and the whole drone group fell 8-15% over two days. AEVEX's own Q2 beat-and-raise was sold by 8%. The stock has already been cut by about half since that print, the Street is bullish, and calls are bid. Positioning is mixed, not a clean crowded short. I found no dated datapoint showing that the price misses something specific. My view is near a coin flip with a slight downside tilt (the peer 2027 pattern, CR caution and Q4-heavy execution risk), and a large two-sided move.

recommendation.reason: The reaction turns on a first combined-company outlook and FY27 framing that no public datapoint pins down. The FY26 raise is mechanical and already in the Street's BlackSea-inclusive numbers. Q3 award flow points to a book-to-bill near 1x, which is what management guided. Peer prints argue mild caution, but not at 65% confidence.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A quantified FY27 framework showing growth (for example combined revenue at or above $800M, with BlackSea named pipeline wins and a Deep Strike follow-on) would make me lean up; an FY27 outlook below the $683M Street figure or a book-to-bill well under 1x would make me lean down.

self_critique: The case for up is real. The stock is half its Q2-print price, the Street is 10 Buy / 1 Hold with targets about twice spot, and a mechanical FY26 raise plus any FY27 growth language ('above-market growth in FY27' was the BlackSea deal pitch) could squeeze a name whose bad news is fully public. The case for down is that the Kratos read-through and the Q2 sell-the-news reaction are clean recent analogues. Either could be right, which is why this is no call.
